prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: The Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests whose Accept header lists only `application/json` (without also listing `text/event-stream`), even though JSON response mode never needs an SSE stream. Both PRs relax the same Accept-header validation check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: The Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests whose Accept header lists only `application/json` (without also listing `text/event-stream`), even though JSON response mode never needs an SSE stream. Both PRs relax the same Accept-header validation check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both patch the identical validation block, but #1996 replaces the naive substring check with a dedicated acceptsMediaType() helper that does real media-range parsing: splits on commas/params, lowercases, and explicitly excludes entries with q=0 and matches type/subtype (with wildcard support) rather than doing plain .includes('application/json'). #2046's visible diff keeps the simpler `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')`-style check, which doesn't account for quality values or wildcard media ranges and is more prone to false positives/negatives on non-trivial Accept headers. #1996 also ships as a standalone helper function, making it easier to unit test the parsing logic in isolation.

prs.title: fix(server): settle pending JSON-mode responses when the streamable HTTP transport closes
prs.author: retif
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves JSON-response-mode POST requests parked forever: handleRequest()'s returned Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down the stream mapping without ever settling that promise, so the HTTP request hangs until the platform's own socket timeout. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves JSON-response-mode POST requests parked forever: handleRequest()'s returned Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down the stream mapping without ever settling that promise, so the HTTP request hangs until the platform's own socket timeout. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs make close() settle the pending Promise<Response> for parked JSON-mode POSTs instead of leaving them hanging, so they fix the same root cause. #2692's fix is narrower and more complete for that specific path: it returns a proper JSON-RPC error envelope (-32000 'Connection closed') per outstanding request id rather than a bare 404, and it explicitly handles the batched-POST case by grouping outstanding ids by stream and reusing any response that already arrived for an id in the batch instead of overwriting it with an error. #2600 answers parked POSTs with a generic 404 'Session not found' and doesn't address the batched multi-id-per-stream case. #2600 also bundles in an unrelated fix (clearing _requestToStreamMapping / a send()-after-storeEvent() correlation leak) that is not part of this overlap and should be filed as its own PR rather than lost when this cluster is consolidated.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs make close() settle the pending Promise<Response> for parked JSON-mode POSTs instead of leaving them hanging, so they fix the same root cause. #2692's fix is narrower and more complete for that specific path: it returns a proper JSON-RPC error envelope (-32000 'Connection closed') per outstanding request id rather than a bare 404, and it explicitly handles the batched-POST case by grouping outstanding ids by stream and reusing any response that already arrived for an id in the batch instead of overwriting it with an error. #2600 answers parked POSTs with a generic 404 'Session not found' and doesn't address the batched multi-id-per-stream case. #2600 also bundles in an unrelated fix (clearing _requestToStreamMapping / a send()-after-storeEvent() correlation leak) that is not part of this overlap and should be filed as its own PR rather than lost when this cluster is consolidated.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs make close() settle the pending Promise<Response> for parked JSON-mode POSTs instead of leaving them hanging, so they fix the same root cause. #2692's fix is narrower and more complete for that specific path: it returns a proper JSON-RPC error envelope (-32000 'Connection closed') per outstanding request id rather than a bare 404, and it explicitly handles the batched-POST case by grouping outstanding ids by stream and reusing any response that already arrived for an id in the batch instead of overwriting it with an error. #2600 answers parked POSTs with a generic 404 'Session not found' and doesn't address the batched multi-id-per-stream case. #2600 also bundles in an unrelated fix (clearing _requestToStreamMapping / a send()-after-storeEvent() correlation leak) that is not part of this overlap and should be filed as its own PR rather than lost when this cluster is consolidated.
